blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, ratios are less individual numbers and more a small dashboard of interlocking signals. The senior finance leader does not watch twenty ratios; they watch six or seven, chosen because together they cover performance, position, efficiency and risk. Each one, on its own, is limited. In combination, they give the leader a confident read on the whole business.

Good dashboards tell a story across time. Six quarters of the same six ratios side by side reveal drift that a single month's numbers hide — a slow erosion in return on capital, a steady rise in receivables days, or a margin that used to move up and down with volume but has quietly been rising for three quarters. That last pattern might signal a genuine strategic improvement, or an accounting change that deserves a closer look.

The point of the dashboard is not to watch numbers. It is to notice the drift early enough that the response can still be calm, and to catch the changes that the rest of the company has not yet felt.

items.q: According to the text, how many ratios does the senior finance leader actually watch?
items.why: "they watch six or seven, chosen because together they cover performance, position, efficiency and risk."

items.q: Why are the ratios chosen as a set rather than individually?
options: To make the report harder to challenge
Because the board prefers longer reports
Because a single ratio is always misleading
Each ratio is limited on its own but together they cover the whole business
items.why: "Each one, on its own, is limited. In combination, they give the leader a confident read on the whole business."

items.q: What does looking at six quarters side by side reveal that a single month hides?
options: The exact cause of every change
Drift — a slow trend across time
Whether the board has read the report
items.why: "Six quarters… side by side reveal drift that a single month's numbers hide."

items.q: The text suggests that a margin quietly rising for three quarters should be…
options: investigated, since it may be strategy OR an accounting change
corrected back to its old range immediately
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o padrão "might signal a genuine strategic improvement, or an accounting change that deserves a closer look" — logo, merece investigação, não aceitação automática.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Trends across quarters matter more than any single month
The real value of a dashboard is spotting drift early
A concise dashboard can outperform an exhaustive one
Adding more ratios always gives the leader a clearer picture
items.why: Inferência: a tese é que o líder observa seis ou sete sinais, não vinte — acrescentar ratios não torna a leitura mais clara.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando o novo painel à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So this is the report I want us to retire. Twenty-two metrics, four pages, and if I'm honest, nobody at board level reads past the first one. It looks thorough. It isn't useful.

What I'm proposing instead fits on a single screen. Six ratios — one each for performance, position, efficiency and risk, plus two I'd defend to anyone. And crucially, each of them shown across the last six quarters, not just this month.

Here's why that matters. Look at receivables days. Any single month, it's within range, nobody blinks. But laid out across six quarters, it has been climbing quietly the whole time. That's cash walking out of the door, and the old report hid it in plain sight.

I'm not asking the board to watch numbers. I'm asking them to notice drift — early enough that we can respond calmly, before it becomes the kind of problem you fix in a panic. The moment a change is loud enough for everyone in the company to feel it, we've already lost the advantage of catching it first.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Harry's main criticism of the old report?
options: It looks thorough but nobody at board level reads past the first metric
It uses the wrong ratios entirely
It is too expensive to produce
It arrives too late each quarter
items.why: "Twenty-two metrics… nobody at board level reads past the first one. It looks thorough. It isn't useful."

items.q: How does Harry propose the six ratios be displayed?
options: One ratio per page for detail
Across the last six quarters, on one screen
Only when a threshold is breached
items.why: "each of them shown across the last six quarters, not just this month."

items.q: Why does Harry use receivables days as his example?
options: Any single month looks fine, but across six quarters it has been climbing quietly
It is the only ratio the board understands
It is the easiest ratio to calculate
items.why: "Any single month, it's within range… But laid out across six quarters, it has been climbing quietly the whole time."

items.q: When Harry says the rising receivables is "cash walking out of the door", he implies that…
options: money is slowly being tied up and effectively lost to the business
the company is deliberately spending more
items.why: Inferência: dias de recebíveis subindo significa caixa preso em contas a receber — dinheiro que deixa de estar disponível.

items.q: What does Harry mean by losing "the advantage of catching it first"?
options: Once a change is obvious to everyone, the chance to respond early and calmly is gone
The report will need to be redesigned again
The board will stop funding the finance team
items.why: Inferência: o valor do painel é notar a deriva antes que ela seja alta o bastante para todos sentirem — depois disso, resta apenas reagir em pânico.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The dashboard is built from interlocking signals, not isolated figures." Interlocking signals are…
options: indicators that only make sense read together
items.why: Interlocking signals = sinais entrelaçados: cada um é limitado sozinho, mas juntos revelam o quadro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Six quarters side by side exposed a slow ___ in return on capital that no single month showed."
items.why: Erosion = erosão: a queda lenta e gradual que só aparece ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "A steady rise in receivables days is a warning sign." Receivables days measure…
options: how long customers take to pay what they owe
the number of trading days in a quarter
the days of stock held in the warehouse
items.why: Receivables days = dias de recebíveis: quanto tempo, em média, os clientes levam para pagar.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Together the ratios give the leader a ___ on the whole business, even though each is limited alone."
items.why: Confident read = leitura segura: a compreensão firme do todo que o conjunto proporciona.

items.q: "The dashboard exists to catch drift early." In this context, drift means…
options: a slow, gradual movement in a trend over time
items.why: Drift = deriva: o deslocamento lento e contínuo que um único mês esconde.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e reporte executivo. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new dashboard before it goes to the board." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the six-ratio format across every business unit next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two board members pushed back on dropping the old twenty-metric report." They…
options: resisted or objected to the idea
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Spotting the drift is useless if we don't follow through on it." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim a ação combinada.

items.q: "Trimming two ratios won't move the needle on how quickly the board reacts." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
